Consonantal i

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Body, health & movement

hit verb

knock against, bump

also bump, bang, hit one’s head, bump into, knock against, stub one’s toe

classical

Quint. 6.3.67: caput … ad fornicem Fabium offendisse
Plaut. Curc. 282: nē quem … capite … offendam

offendō, offendere, offendī, offēnsum

verb, third conjugation

knock, bump (a part of the body, or someone)

The part of the body is the object, with ad and what it hits (caput, pedem offendere); or the person bumped is the object and the part of the body is in the ablative (Plaut. Curc. 282).

Other words

  • illīdō, illīdere, illīsī, illīsum — dash, bang (against)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Suet. Aug. 23: caput foribus (Lewis & Short)

    (plērumque poētica; in Cicerōnis ōrātiōne solūtā nōn invenītur (Lewis & Short))

Examples

  • nē quem in cursū capite aut cubitō aut pectore offendam aut genū

    so that I don’t bump into anyone with my head or elbow or chest or knee as I runPlaut. Curc. 282

  • caput eum ad fornicem Fabium offendisse

    that he had hit his head on the Arch of Fabius (Cicero’s joke about a very tall man)Quint. 6.3.67

  • In manibus portābunt tē, nē forte offendās ad lapidem pedem tuum.

    They will carry you in their hands, so that you do not strike your foot against a stone.Vulg. Ps. 90 (91), 12

  • Cavē nē caput offendās.

    Mind you don’t bump your head.composed

See also bump, strike, fall, meet.

SourcesLewis & Short: offendo · Lewis & Short: illido
